title: Settlement Conditions for a Picked-Up Trade-In Agreement
content:
A picked-up **Trade-In Agreements** agreement is settled when three conditions hold together.

**Rule.** A picked-up agreement is settled when all three hold: the lien payoff has been sent or there was no lien, the title received date is recorded, and the equity balance is exactly zero. An agreement with a negative balance stays open until the shortfall is covered; one with a positive balance stays open until the equity is applied or paid out.

All three conditions are read from Kestrel's own agreement record: its lienholder, its title received date and its undistributed trade equity.

## The three conditions

| Condition | Met when |
|---|---|
| Lien | The lien payoff has been sent, or the agreement names no lienholder |
| Title | A title received date is recorded on the agreement |
| Equity | The undistributed trade equity is exactly $0.00 |

## Decision table

| Lien condition | Title condition | Equity balance | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Met | Met | Exactly zero | Settled |
| Any | Any | Below zero | Stays open until the shortfall is covered |
| Any | Any | Above zero | Stays open until the equity is applied or paid out |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical)

- An unliened agreement with a title received date and a balance of $0.00 meets all three conditions.
- A balance of $0.01 is not exactly zero; the agreement stays open until that equity is applied or paid out.
